affected_claim: Uncertainty around the estimated output response to personal-income-tax cuts.
evidence_summary: 2016 WP p.22: personal-tax cut output response becomes non-significant even with 68% intervals, where original wild-bootstrap95% intervals excluded zero. Peak (third-step) corrected68% output interval is [−.3%,2.8%] with corporate tax ordered first, versus [−2.9%,4.0%] for the opposite ordering. These two corrected intervals are different identification orderings, not an old/new pair. Reply pp.6–7 confirms wild-bootstrap intervals narrower and MBB includes zero at every displayed output horizon, but other valid inference methods retain significance. Monte Carlo original nominal95% coverage16–18% versus MBB91–92% is a simulation finding, not an empirical effect estimate.
dispute_status: Full author reply recovered. Printed p.2 explicitly acknowledges wild bootstrap not generally asymptotically valid. Authors defend significant effects under delta method/parametric bootstrap and explain that some critique intervals reflect combined tax changes.
